notes: Ethereum mainnet contracts-only MUGI V1 launch: the initial IMD transaction creates exactly these four full-code factories in manifest order. Each nonpayable constructor takes only $owner, resolving to 0x20714d50f4675c366de30b603728a90ddddb240f; none creates children, calls dependencies or checks external code. Preserve the accepted source and Solidity 0.8.26, Cancun, optimizer 200, viaIR and bytecode_hash none. The main factory constructor pins the hash and length of the exact raw hook creation code, excluding constructor arguments. All nineteen later descendants are disclosed for audit and admission: ten MugiIMDCrewToken instances, MugiIMDGameHook, MugiAirdrop, MugiIMDSwapRouter, MugiVRFAdapter, MugiIMDVerifier, MugiIMDLedger, MugiIMDBuybacks, MugiIMDPriceOracle and MugiIMDV4Engine. Five separate owner transactions later create service modules, crews, engine, accounting modules and finally the hook. Fixed CREATE nonces predict dependencies; service-module creation commits the complete fourteen-static-field hook initcode hash and mined CREATE2 salt. deployHook verifies that commitment and the constructor-pinned raw code. All child constructor arguments are static; no application initialize/configure/bindAccounting or dependency replacement is available. Economic activation validates reciprocal bindings, token identity and ledger exclusions. Final graph addresses, service coordinator/subscription, attestor and signer settings require a reviewed subsequent deployment plan; mock values are forbidden for live operation. This request deploys no descendants and seeds no pools. Registry entries index only the four factories; their creation does not deploy or activate the whole game. No standard token launch, distributor, swarm allocation, proxy, delegatecall route, token-launch economics, deployment ETH funding or initialization calls. V1 retains ten crews, initial 95/5 LP/airdrop allocation, scheduled daily cutoffs, nine VRF eliminations, 75% loser conversions, pro-rata treasures, LP redistribution, bounded buybacks, team fees, timeout recovery and thirty-day final claims. Each crew token creates its entire finite reserve once in its constructor, has no external mint and burns only the caller's balance. totalSupply includes unused reserve and is not circulating supply; unused reserve is excluded from eligibility and burned on elimination, ordinary finale or emergency closure. Ledger exclusions include all PoolManager custody, including third-party v4 pools. Transfers remain free at cutoff and after elimination, with no holder confiscation, hook token callbacks or owner trading pause. Snapshots strictly before scheduled cutoffs preserve earned rights. Official-pool swaps require a live crew, Live phase and time before cutoff; token reward materialization waits during resolution and resumes in eligible phases within claim deadlines. These gates restrict game venues and reward timing, not ERC20 transfers. V2 is separate future work: after ordinary finale, unused reserve is retired and V1 retains player token backing and reserved player/team ETH. An owner-only one-shot atomic handoff sends only available inventory/ETH to a deployed receiveV1Finale(uint8,address,uint256) receiver. A zero constructor target permits future owner selection; a nonzero pin is enforced. Receiver failure rolls back the handoff; V1 claims continue and emergency closure cannot migrate. Finale residual assets are not a new holder reward and depend on owner action, with no permissionless handoff fallback; no automatic wallet-level V2 allocation is promised. See ADAPTATION.md and docs/IMD_CONSTRUCTOR_DEPLOYMENT.md for trust and eligibility disclosures. Remote admission, IMD launch record, factory addresses and receipts remain unproven until the deployment service confirms them. No explorer source verification is authorized; if mandatory, stop for requester input before deployment.
